tips.text: In decomposition, explicitly split the problem into subproblems and solve each before assembling the full design; a candidate's feedback flagged skipping this step.
Do not second-guess a correct solution without evidence; one candidate's hesitation on a topological-sort problem read as feigned difficulty.
In the learning round ask high-level clarifying questions; questions that suggest you need step-by-step guidance can sink the round.
Take clear positions in design rounds and defend them; a working solution beats an unfinished optimized one.
Prepare SQL and decomposition, not just algorithms; coding rounds stressed object structure and clean code more than algorithms.
SQL can appear in the learning round even for candidates told no preparation is needed.
Treat decomposition differently from a system design interview, but know system design concepts.
Practice reading unfamiliar code and debugging under time pressure, and tie every decision to the customer outcome.
Deployment Strategist: decomposition is not a consulting case; drive toward metrics, data sources, a test query and a pilot.
Use Foundry before interviewing (a free AIP Developer Tier exists); treating the company as a black box reads poorly.
Narrate each step during the query-language round and absorb corrections without repeating the mistake.
Casual conversations during the process are evaluative too.
Expect a possible multi-week wait after the hiring manager round.
Ask for a referral if you can; one candidate who applied cold regretted not doing so.

tips.text: Decomp matters most: treat the interviewer as the client and pin down stakeholder, scope and KPI before discussing architecture.
In decomp, design application-first, then data/ETL; add ML only if the use case needs it. Stay high-level and skip caching or sharding detail.
Coding is practical and easier than LeetCode; keep it simple with dicts, strings and lists, ask clarifying questions and narrate. Interviewers weigh thought process heavily.
Lead with your strongest of applications, data and GenAI; breadth matters but interviewers look for depth somewhere.
Map behavioral stories to specific Databricks core values (customer obsessed, truth seeking, first principles, bias for action, etc.).
AI FDE candidates should ask the recruiter early whether to prepare for LLM or classical ML system design.
Build something small on the free Databricks edition to learn the platform before the loop.
Expect process churn: candidates report the loop being revamped, and RSA loops being converted to FDE loops midway.
One 2026 candidate found Databricks' own prep materials detailed; ask your recruiter for them.
